methodology.metaTitle: Domlivo Price Index: methodology and open data
methodology.metaDescription: How the Domlivo Price Index of asking prices in Albania is computed: sample, filters, median and range, the 30-flat rule, how to cite it, CSV and JSON.
methodology.h1: Domlivo Price Index: how the figures are computed
methodology.lead: The median asking price per square metre of flats and studios listed for sale on Domlivo, by city and district in Albania, recomputed every hour from the live listings. Free to reuse under CC BY 4.0.
methodology.figuresLead: Computed on {date}. A city with fewer than {min} flats in the sample shows its size instead of a headline figure.
methodology.figuresCaption: Domlivo Price Index by city, {date}: median and 20th-80th percentile asking price per m² of flats and studios listed for sale on Domlivo
methodology.askingBody: The price a seller or an agency states in a listing. It is not the price a sale closed at: the two can differ, and the index measures only the first.
methodology.sampleBody: Listings published on domlivo.com, active and offered for sale at the moment of computation. The price figures use flats and studios only; houses, villas, land and commercial space count towards the number of listings, not towards the prices.
methodology.filtersBody: A listing without a price is left out. For a listing priced per m² the stated rate is used; otherwise the total asking price is divided by the floor area. An area under 15 m² is treated as a data error and left out of the per-m² figures.
methodology.thresholdBody: A median over fewer than {min} flats is never shown as a headline figure. Pages say "too little data" with the number of flats, tables mark it with an asterisk, and the downloads flag it (low_sample).
methodology.medianBody: The median is the middle value of the per-m² prices (the mean of the two middle values when their number is even), rounded to the euro. The range is the 20th to the 80th percentile, interpolated linearly, so one mistyped price does not move it.
methodology.frequencyBody: Recomputed from the live listings at most once an hour, and every figure carries the date it was computed on. A monthly edition is published in the blog only when the figures have changed since the previous one.
methodology.researchBody: Zone tables with a confidence column report published market research, cited with its sources beside the table. They are not part of the index and can differ from it.
methodology.citeBody: Name the index, the place, the date of the figures and the page you took them from:
methodology.licenceBody: The figures and the files are published under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0: copy, share and adapt them, commercially too, with credit to the Domlivo Price Index and a link.
methodology.downloadsBody: Regenerated hourly with the pages. The CSV has one file per city, the whole city first and then its districts; the JSON holds every city and district with a description of each field.

purchase.metaTitle: Property purchase cost calculator for Albania
purchase.metaDescription: What buying a flat in Albania costs on top of the price: notary, ASHK registration, lawyer, sworn translator and agency fee. Enter the price and see each line.
purchase.h1: Property purchase cost calculator for Albania
purchase.lead: What buying a flat or a house in Albania costs on top of the price: the notary, registration of ownership with the cadastre (ASHK), a lawyer if you want one, a sworn translator and the agency fee. Enter the price to see each line and the total. The buyer pays no transfer tax, so there is no line for one.
purchase.linkText: Property purchase cost calculator for Albania
purchase.totalNote: The total is the sum of the lines above, and the share of the price is that total divided by the price.
purchase.noTransferTax: There is no transfer tax line: an individual buying a flat pays none. The costs of owning the flat afterwards, such as the annual building tax, are not part of the purchase.
purchase.faq1q: How much does it cost to buy a flat in Albania on top of the price?
purchase.faq1a: For a flat at {price}, the calculator adds {total}, or {pct} of the price: {lines}.
purchase.faq2q: Does the buyer pay a transfer tax in Albania?
purchase.faq2a: No. An individual buying a flat pays no transfer tax, so the calculator has no line for it: the tax on the sale is the seller's. Read the contract all the same, because a clause can move the seller's costs to the buyer.
purchase.faq3q: Do I need a lawyer and a sworn translator?
purchase.faq3a: A lawyer is not required by law, but recommended: a check of the title, encumbrances and permits costs about €500-2,000, and the calculator counts {lawyer}. A sworn translator is required if you don't speak Albanian. The translator co-signs the deed with you and charges about €50-150; the calculator counts {translator}.
purchase.faq4q: Who registers the ownership, and what does it cost?
purchase.faq4a: The notary files the registration with the state cadastre (ASHK) for you, for a fixed fee of about {registration}. The notary's own fee follows the official scale, about 0.30-0.35% of the price (Ministry of Justice Order 279/2012).

rental.metaDescription: Gross and net rental yield of a flat in Albania, let long-term or short-term, after letting costs, management, running costs and the {tax} tax.
rental.lead: Work out the gross and net yield of a flat in Albania, let long-term or to holiday guests. The calculator takes off letting costs, management, running costs and the {tax} tax on rental income. The presets hold our estimates for a one-bedroom flat in Durrës; choose manual input to enter your own figures.
rental.methodGross: Long let: the monthly rent × 12. Short let: the nightly rate × the nights let, which are 365 × occupancy, capped by the season limit if you set one.
rental.methodLet: Long let: one empty month a year and half a month's rent to the letting agent. Short let: {platform} in platform fees and {localTax} tourist tax on the gross income.
rental.methodMgmt: The fee you set, as a share of the gross income: 0% if you manage the flat yourself.
rental.methodRunning: Repairs at {repairs} of the price a year, insurance and building tax at {fixed} a year; short lets add {utilities} a year for utilities.
rental.methodTax: {tax} of the gross income less the letting or platform costs.
rental.methodGrossYield: Gross income divided by the price.
rental.methodNetYield: Net income divided by the price plus the buying costs: {buyPct} of the price and {buyFixed} for the notary, agency, ASHK registration, lawyer and translator, as in the purchase cost calculator.
rental.presetsNote: A preset fills in the rent, occupancy, season and management fee; manual input lets you change each of them.
rental.faq1q: How is rental income taxed in Albania?
rental.faq1a: At {tax}, for long and short lets alike. The calculator applies it to the gross rent less the letting or platform costs.
rental.faq2q: What is the difference between gross and net yield?
rental.faq2a: Gross yield is a year's rent divided by the price. Net yield is what is left after letting costs, management, running costs and tax, divided by the price plus the buying costs.
rental.faq2Example: For the long-let preset at {price}: {gross} gross, {net} net.
rental.faq3q: Which earns more, a long-term or a short-term let?
rental.faq3a: With our presets for a one-bedroom flat in Durrës at {price}, the calculator gives these net yields: {list}.
rental.faq4q: Where do the preset figures come from?
rental.faq4a: They are Domlivo estimates of October 2026 for a one-bedroom flat in Durrës: {str} for short lets and {ltr} for a long let. They are not a guarantee of income; switch to manual input to try your own figures.

About.metaTitle: About Domlivo: the team and how the site works
About.metaDescription: Who builds Domlivo, the property marketplace for Albania: the three founders, where the listings come from, how they are kept current and how to reach us.
About.intro1: Domlivo is a property marketplace for Albania. It lists apartments, houses, villas, land and commercial space for sale in Durrës, Tirana, Vlorë, Sarandë and along the coast, for buyers from abroad and for people who already live here.
About.intro2: Listings come from owners and partner agencies. Every listing states its price and who is offering the property; you talk to them directly, and Domlivo adds no commission of its own. The site is available in seven languages: Albanian, English, Ukrainian, Russian, Italian, Polish and German.

mission.title: Our idea
mission.body1: We are building Domlivo as a decentralised, analytical AI marketplace for property in Albania. The aim is simple: a buyer finds a suitable listing quickly and gets a consultation from an AI assistant right in the chat. The assistant answers from Domlivo's own research documents: what utilities cost, what an investment returns, what a purchase costs on top of the price.
mission.body2: Decentralised means something specific here. The catalogue does not belong to one agency: owners and many partner agencies publish on it, each listing names who listed it, and the buyer talks to that lister directly.
mission.uspTitle: What is on the site today

usp.item1: AI search: describe the home in your own words; the assistant searches the listings and answers from Domlivo's research, citing its sources.
usp.item2: Guides where every figure has a source and a date.
usp.item3: Asking prices by district on city pages, recalculated every hour from live listings.
usp.item4: A “what it costs to buy and own” block on listing pages.
usp.item5: Seven languages and a currency switcher.
usp.item6: Side-by-side comparisons of districts and cities.
usp.item7: Direct contact with owners and agencies, no commission.

research.title: Research, with sources
research.body: Next to the listings we publish market research: buying guides, a blog and price pages for cities and districts. Figures come from a named source with a date, and where we have no data the page says so.

team.title: The team
team.intro: Domlivo was started by three people. One sells property in Albania every day; the other two build websites for a living.

fedir.bio: Analyst and marketer. He builds the Domlivo platform and the market research published on it: the price pages, the guides and the data behind them. Tech lead and founder of the web studio Code-Site.

viktor.bio: He lives in Albania and runs the agency Grinchenko Real Estate. Over the last few years he has sold more than 100 apartments here, and he helps buyers with documents, renting a property out and the questions that come up after a purchase. He founded a popular Telegram channel about Albania. His rule is to visit every flat in person and tell viewers the truth about it, the pluses and the minuses.

diana.bio: She is responsible for the design, packaging and user experience of Domlivo; the ideas that turn a visit into an enquiry are hers. Lead designer at Code-Site. Her view is that design has to sell, so she thinks about conversion before she thinks about grids and colours.

listings.title: How listings get on Domlivo
listings.intro: We would rather describe what actually happens than promise more than we do.
listings.item1: Listings are added by property owners and by partner agencies and realtors who register on the site.
listings.item2: When an agency or a realtor lists a property, the listing names them next to the price.
listings.item3: The price is stated in the listing. When a property is sold or withdrawn, the listing leaves the catalogue.
listings.item4: Seen a listing that is out of date or wrong? Write to us and we will check it with whoever posted it.
